title: TOIL Analytics
body:
Benedict has asked that we figure out a way to see who is using toil besides us.

┆Issue is synchronized with this [JIRA Epic](https://ucsc-cgl.atlassian.net/browse/TOIL-419)
┆Issue Number: TOIL-419
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: We have Google Analytics set up on the Toil ReadTheDocs and landing page that might help with this.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
I think it might be possible to feed events in to Google Analytics without collecting any personally identifiable information (and hence triggering the need for a privacy policy that covers installing Toil, among other obligations).

The [Measurement Protocol](https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/collection/protocol/v1/devguide) would be the way to go. It requires [an `Anonymous Client ID` or `User ID`](https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/collection/protocol/v1/parameters#user), which they seem to think can be a unique value stored either on the user's device or on our system while simultaneously remaining non-identifying. I'm not sure how they come to that conclusion; surely if I have your ID number and your device also has your ID number, I can identify you by checking what ID number you have stored on your device.

Anyway, we could either lump all the hits together under one fake user, or use completely ephemeral IDs and try to stop the user's system from logging its own ID.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: Not sure that we're going to do this.  We can always reopen it if we reevaluate.
